Solution: Add hard _simulationScheduled guard to TryWriteEditorTuning, TryReadEditorTuning, TryGetEditorMeshSnapshot, and ApplyPendingEditorTuningImmediate. Writes still sanitize and stage static pending values, but immediate vault mutation is deferred until ApplyQualityAndEditorTuning runs in normal pre-simulation boundary.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling JobHandle.Complete() from editor code was rejected because it would serialize pipeline and violate native job mandate. Returning live read-only alias while job is active was rejected because vertex buffer is still producer target. second editor snapshot buffer was rejected because it adds persistent memory for debug-only facade.
Problem: CSV hot-reload was guarded by UNITY_EDITOR DEVELOPMENT_BUILD, so development player could execute periodic File.Exists, File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc, and FileStream work from PreSimulationTick. parser itself is byte/span based, but filesystem probe is still disallowed in gameplay runtime cadence.
Solution: Restrict MonitorBeamCsv and its pre-simulation polling call to #if UNITY_EDITOR only. human-facing editor bridge remains intact; player and development gameplay builds keep unmanaged scalar DTO path but do not poll filesystem.

SHINOBU_71 Rationale
Status: STATIC VERIFIED / BUILD HELD BY GUARD
Decision 001 - Attach DRS To Existing Adapter
Problem: repository already contains ThermalDynamicResolutionAdapter and DynamicResolutionScaler; adding third scaler would create competing render-scale writers.
Solution: Keep ownership in existing graphics scalability adapter and patch only missing SHINOBU_71 acceptance gaps.
Rejected Alternatives: new MonoBehaviour would race existing adapter and duplicate DynamicResolutionHandler state. Direct Screen.SetResolution is forbidden because it reallocates display buffers.
Scalability potential: Low keeps scale near survival floor with sharpened reconstruction; Middle/High recover smoothly; Ultra spends headroom on visual overkill shader globals.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids display-buffer reallocations and keeps DRS work scalar-only; estimated hot-path cost remains below 100 microseconds, pending profiler proof.
Decision 002 - Cache GlobalQualityWeight From Vault Contract
Problem: adapter had stress-derived quality proxy, so DRS could pass static scans while not explicitly consuming published GlobalQualityWeight scalar.
Solution: Cache sanitized global quality scalar once per Tick from BufferID.ShinobuScalabilityState / ScalabilityStateDTO.GlobalQualityWeight, fall back only to last valid cached quality/default 1.0 when vault handle is absent, let mock quality weight clamp it, and use TargetRenderScale = lerp(minScaleLimit, 1.0, cachedWeight) before existing pressure collapses. Expose cached scalar in ResolutionScaleState at offset 52 without growing 64 B contract.
Rejected Alternatives: Native Shader.GetGlobalFloat reads were rejected because they cross into presentation state from policy Tick. Creating scalability dictator buffer from DRS was rejected because DRS does not own that domain's memory.
Scalability potential: Low uses same continuous scalar to fall toward survival scale. Middle rises smoothly without threshold chatter. High keeps scale close to 1.0 while still reducing post/shader pressure under stress. Ultra uses headroom for visual-overkill globals instead of separate binary branch.
Hardware Impact: Removes two shader-global native bridge reads from Tick and avoids concrete Homeostasis polling in policy fallback. Vault handle resolution is cached; estimated hot-path source read remains sub-1 us. preserved render-scale drop can save 500-3000 us GPU fill time under pressure, scene dependent, not profiler-measured in this pass.
Decision 003 - Repair No-Runtime URP Fallback
Problem: adapter fallback accepted render-scale parameter but discarded it, only resizing scalable buffers. If IDynamicResolutionRuntime is absent, URP asset scale could remain stale.
Solution: In ApplyDirectRenderScale, clamp render scale, write _urpAsset.renderScale only when value changes beyond epsilon, then resize scalable buffers with sanitized buffer scale. existing registry runtime remains normal writer.
Rejected Alternatives: Allocating replacement render targets was rejected for GC/VRAM churn. Forcing Screen.SetResolution was rejected for display-buffer stutter. Writing URP asset every frame was rejected because epsilon-gated writes are cheaper.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle keep survival scale even if registry runtime is missing. High/Ultra keep 1.0 scale without extra writes. All tiers preserve same shader global contract.
Hardware Impact: Fallback branch adds one float compare and rare property write; sub-2 us CPU when active. Prevents stale full-resolution rendering that can cost 500-3000 us GPU on i3/MX350 pressure scenes.
Decision 004 - Keep Upscaling Tiered And Screen-Space Only
Problem: uniform FSR path can burn compute on mobile/low-tier hardware, and tying DRS to AUP/world coordinates would widen screen-space system for no gain.
Solution: Keep existing tier resolver: native at full scale, bilinear/TAA for low/mobile/no-compute, FSR hash only when hardware tier and compute support justify it. Publish screen pixel dimensions and post-process weight as shader globals; keep DRS state to scalar screen-space fields.
Rejected Alternatives: FSR on Quest/MX350-class weak ALUs was rejected because compute reconstruction can erase fill-rate savings. Passing AUP doubles into DRS was rejected because render scale is camera/screen-space, not world-space.

Solution: Patch existing Merkle sub-block job and binary manifest in place. Keep pager RLE path intact. Use existing GlobalDataVault buffers and WAL validation.
Rejected Alternatives: New RleWalCompressor service, second WAL file, or parallel save manager; all would create split recovery semantics and higher integration risk with 20+ agents.
Scalability potential: Low devices get RLE wins on empty/repeated payloads; middle devices fall back to LZ4 for mixed payloads; high devices keep richer cosmetic payloads through continuous thresholds; ultra devices spend saved I/O budget on denser state persistence instead of stalling.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350 with MicroSD, expected gain is reduced worker write bytes for repetitive inventories/voxels. CPU cost is one linear worker-side scan per sub-block; no main-thread dependency added.
Decision 02: Literal ARM64 SectorEntryDTO
Problem: Prompt required exact SectorEntryDTO field names/types, but Merkle code had internal SectorEntry with signed long fields.
Solution: Rename only Merkle directory DTO to SectorEntryDTO, change two 8-byte fields to ulong, and update BinaryLayoutManifest plus emergency header size.
Rejected Alternatives: Leave meaning-equivalent signed fields; violates literal prompt and can hide directory sign bugs. Changing SaveBinaryStorage.SectorEntry; rejected because that is separate V10 storage DTO with its own compatibility shim.
Scalability potential: Low/middle devices scan aligned 32B entries without traps; high/ultra devices can scale sector counts without layout ambiguity.
Hardware Impact: Directory scans stay 8-byte aligned for ARM64/Quest-class CPUs. Estimated gain is small per entry, but it removes hard crash class.

Problem: Autosaves on slow MicroSD freeze when raw or weakly compressed repetitive state reaches WAL. existing sub-block job was LZ4/raw only.
Solution: Add Lz4BlockFlagRle and Burst-safe RLE pass inside Lz4SubBlockCompressionJob; use RLE only when smaller than raw, otherwise use existing LZ4/raw fallback and CRC validation.
Rejected Alternatives: Replace LZ4 with pure RLE; bad for mixed entropy payloads. Add second NativeList compressor; duplicate memory and recovery semantics.

Solution: Change SHINOBU_72 SaveSystem Burst jobs to FloatMode.Deterministic while keeping CompileSynchronously = true and FloatPrecision.Standard.
Rejected Alternatives: Change only float-heavy job; rejected because future edit can add float math to integer-named save job and silently reintroduce fast-math drift. Leave Fast for speed; rejected for co-op rollback correctness.
Problem: StateDeltaRecordDTO headers inside delta byte arena were copied as raw host-memory structs. vault DTO layout is aligned, but WAL payload bytes must be archive contract, not x86/ARM little-endian accident.
Solution: Keep StateDeltaRecordDTO as 64B field-only NativeArray DTO for Burst/editor inspection, but write/read arena header through explicit little-endian helpers. Rejected Alternatives: Leave raw UnsafeUtility.MemCpy(&record) because current hardware is little-endian; rejected because WAL deltas are persistent data. Add managed serializer; rejected because it violates zero-GC and duplicates binary contract.
Problem: GenerateEmergencyMockHeader() still computed CRC and copied SaveMerkleEmergencyHeader64 from host struct memory. This is cold fallback, but it is still binary header used when legacy archaeology is absent.
Solution: Emit 64B emergency header through explicit little-endian byte writes, compute CRC over those canonical bytes with Checksum=0, then rewrite checksum and copy canonical bytes to caller buffer. Manifest coverage now asserts every emergency header field offset.
Rejected Alternatives: Leave it as raw struct because path is cold; rejected because fallback headers must be less fragile than normal headers. Add second emergency-header DTO; rejected under duplicate-contract ban.
Problem: Validation proved WAL records were intact, but Merkle WAL side did not expose zero-GC recovery path that decodes stored raw/RLE/LZ4 sub-blocks back into delta arena. save system that only validates compressed bytes cannot honestly claim replay readiness.
Solution: Add TryReplayWalToDeltaArena() as cold recovery helper. It reads canonical WAL headers, verifies record CRC over canonical bytes, rejects overlapping destination/scratch buffers, decodes sub-blocks into caller-owned NativeArray delta arena using caller-owned compressed scratch, and records replay counters without allocating byte. Corrupt mod records are skipped; corrupt core records fail.
Rejected Alternatives: Use editor window as replay path; rejected because recovery must be callable from boot/runtime code. Allocate managed payload arrays while replaying; rejected because WAL recovery should not create GC pressure on crash startup. Duplicate pager WAL reader; rejected under duplicate WAL law.

SHINOBU_73 Rationale
Initial Architectural Decisions
Problem: Vault hot data needs anti-tamper validation without managed obfuscation or runtime reflection scanners.
Solution: Use Vault-owned unmanaged buffers, Burst pointer-span hashing, typed SignalBus lanes, previous-frame VisualSync completion, and fixed-size telemetry.
Rejected Alternatives: Managed C# obfuscators and object graph scanners allocate, miss NativeArray payloads, and are trivial to bypass by patching managed metadata.
Scalability potential: Low = sparse cadence and critical targets only; Middle = inventory + AUP + selected Vault buffers; High = deeper target set; Ultra = aggressive cadence and larger rollback mirrors.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 target is bounded by cadence and byte budget, with validation work shifted to jobs and completion delayed to next VisualSync frame.
Problem: Desync correction must be invisible for inventory tamper and teleport edits.
Solution: Keep last valid byte mirrors in Vault memory, correct mutated bytes after validation mismatch, and emit typed signals for diagnostics.
Rejected Alternatives: Immediate gameplay-visible lockout on first mismatch would expose sentinel and create false positives on legal state changes.
Scalability potential: Low = rollback only for critical spans; Middle = rollback plus hash delta updates; High/Ultra = more spans and richer telemetry.
Hardware Impact: Copy cost is proportional to span size and capped by fixed rollback capacity.
Problem: Legal inventory/AUP changes must not look like cheats.
Solution: Consume typed hash-delta updates and AUP shift signals; only unannounced direct byte changes trigger rollback.
Rejected Alternatives: Hash-only comparison without semantic update path would punish legitimate gameplay and save/load transitions.
Scalability potential: Same DTO and signal lanes scale from one mock span to many registered target spans.
Hardware Impact: Signal reads are snapshot spans; no managed allocations in hot path.
Problem: Validator state must survive context compression and concurrent agent work.
Solution: Store task state and rationale in Docs/Tasks and Docs/AgentLogs before code edits.
Rejected Alternatives: Chat-only status is not authoritative under batch protocol.
Scalability potential: Enables integrator to audit progress without replaying chat.
Hardware Impact: Documentation only; no runtime impact.
Decision 001 - Assembly Boundary Split
Problem: Core/Memory asmdef owns GlobalDataVault contracts but cannot reference GlobalRegistry/SystemDispatcher without cyclic assembly dependency.

Rejected Alternatives: Fabricating old binary key layout would be false evidence. Using managed arrays would violate DataVault sovereignty.
Problem: Memory edits happen in unmanaged NativeArray/Vault spans where C# obfuscators and reflection scanners do not prove integrity.
Solution: Burst IJobParallelFor consumes raw void* spans and uses Unity.Mathematics.xxHash3.Hash64, folding to StoredHash while retaining FullHash64 telemetry.
Rejected Alternatives: CRC32-only, reflection, managed heap scanners, or string event reports.
Hardware Impact: Target budget is <0.2 ms aggregate by byte budget and cadence. Exact saved microseconds are not claimed without profiler capture.
Problem: Inventory tamper should not surface as visible lockout when last legal byte mirror is available.
Solution: Maintain Vault-owned rollback bytes and MemCpy back over tampered span when mismatch is correctable.
Rejected Alternatives: Throwing on every mismatch creates false positives for legal gameplay and exposes sentinel behavior.
Problem: raw hash mismatch catches byte edits but not all semantically impossible teleports if another system writes new legal-looking AUP.
Solution: Store previous PlayerKinematicState AUP, compare double3 delta/required speed, allow AupShiftSignal and PlayerTransportBailoutSignal, then clamp back on illegal jumps.
Rejected Alternatives: Transform.position checks are not authoritative in HECTON-8. Hashing downcast floats would miss double precision tamper.
Problem: Modded sectors must mutate without disabling base-game integrity.
Solution: Allow skip only for target ranges with MODP/0x4D50 prefix and nonzero ModdedGameMask.
Rejected Alternatives: global modded-game bypass would remove economy/player protection that matters.
Problem: prompt asks for GlobalRegistry FunctionPointer validation, but no exposed unmanaged registry segment is available without inventing dependency.
Solution: Implement pointer fingerprint validation for every internal target record: pointer + byte length + buffer id are checked in Burst before hashing.
Rejected Alternatives: Scanning managed GlobalRegistry internals or inventing fake FunctionPointer array would be unverifiable and fragile.
Decision 008 - Verification Wall
Problem: Local compile verification could not reach SHINOBU files through generated project files.
Solution: Ran dotnet and Unity batch attempts, recorded objective blockers, and did not claim green Unity compile.
Rejected Alternatives: Reporting success from stale generated csproj would be fake; patching EconomyRuntimeInstaller is outside SHINOBU_73 domain.
Problem: first runtime draft referenced Hecton8.Gameplay.PlayerKinematicState, but BufferID.PlayerKinematicState is actually written by Core lockstep path as LockstepPlayerKinematicState.
Solution: Remove Gameplay namespace dependency and consume existing Core determinism vault contract for that buffer. Reconstruct absolute meters from sector/local using HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble, then write sector/local back only on rollback.
Rejected Alternatives: local 96-byte mirror looked cleaner but would fail DataVault alignment validation because vault stores both stride and alignment. Transform.position was rejected because it is not AUP authority.
Problem: Default BurstCompile leaves compile timing and float mode implicit, and unannotated NativeArray fields make Burst assume pointer aliasing.
Solution: Add CompileSynchronously = true, FloatMode.Deterministic, FloatPrecision.Standard, and field-level NoAlias to validation and mock mutation jobs.
Rejected Alternatives: FloatMode.Fast is acceptable for visual-only math, but this lane touches lockstep rollback evidence. Default alias assumptions would reduce vectorization confidence.
Hardware Impact: Protects NEON/AVX vectorization eligibility. Exact microseconds saved require Unity profiler/Burst disassembly.
Problem: _lockedBuffers = new BufferID was managed private field in sentinel driver.
Solution: Replace it with FixedList128Bytes, enough for fixed target budget without heap allocation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping array as cold enough weakens Vault-law audit and creates false positive for managed state.
Decision 012 - Unity Compile Wall Evidence
Problem: Unity batch compile terminates before import/compile while another Unity process owns project lock.
Solution: Preserve logs and mark Unity verification blocked by existing editor process/Temp/UnityLockfile; do not kill developer tooling.
Rejected Alternatives: Killing Unity would risk developer's open scene/inspector state. Claiming compile success from dotnet build would be false because generated csproj excludes new SHINOBU files.
Scalability potential: None; verification only.
Problem: MemoryDesyncSignal and HashDeltaUpdateSignal originally lived under Core runtime files, forcing peer domains to reference Core if they wanted to publish legal hash deltas.
Solution: Move SHINOBU signal payloads to Hecton8.Core.Contracts assembly while leaving SignalBus storage/driver in Core runtime. payloads stay unmanaged and 64-byte padded.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping signals in Core runtime would create exactly compile-wall coupling mandate forbids. Moving full SignalBus into Contracts would be broad architecture change outside SHINOBU scope.
Problem: initial kernel only wrote result flags and let runtime publish desyncs after job completion. That was defensible for correction, but it was not literal enough for Task 06.
Solution: Pass NativeQueue.ParallelWriter into MemorySentinelValidationJob and enqueue mismatch/invalid-pointer signals directly from Burst kernel. Runtime keeps secondary desync emission only for rollback/fatal context.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling SignalBus.Push from Core.Memory job would introduce Core runtime dependency and is not Burst-safe static call boundary. Duplicating every signal in runtime was rejected as telemetry noise.
Problem: Quality cadence used linear lerp only, which lacked mandated polynomial breathing curve and explicit math.step collapse.
Solution: Use smoothstep polynomial q*q*(3-2q) before math.lerp for validation cadence, and math.step for per-target MinQualityWeight gating inside Burst kernel.
Rejected Alternatives: Binary if low-end switches and linear-only cadence scaling create either abrupt protection changes or noncompliant quality behavior.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 reduces bytes hashed by skipping high-min-quality targets and increasing cadence frames; no exact microseconds claimed without profiler capture.
Problem: job-side desync lane reported invalid pointers and content hash mismatches, but pointer/fingerprint mismatch flags could remain silent when pointed bytes still hashed to expected value.
Solution: Route hash mismatch, pointer mismatch, and pointer-fingerprint mismatch through one post-hash MemoryDesyncSignal gate after ExpectedHash and StoredHash are finalized.
Rejected Alternatives: Hash-only emission misses target-record tampering. Runtime-only emission would defer evidence outside Burst validation kernel and duplicate Loop 7 fault-lane correction.
Hardware Impact: Normal frame cost is unchanged. Tamper frame cost is one NativeQueue enqueue for structural mismatch; exact microseconds require Unity profiler capture.
Decision 017 - Prompt-Exact Status Renumbering
Problem: implementation status split Task 06 signal emission into separate checklist item and shifted Tasks 07-17 away from XML assignment, making audit harder to verify mechanically.
Solution: Rewrite checklist items 06-17 to match original SHINOBU_73 prompt numbering exactly while preserving same DOD evidence.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving shifted checklist would be functionally harmless for code but noncompliant with batch protocol's task reconciliation requirement.
Problem: Manual Roslyn probe caught 0x494E565F484F545F31UL, 9-byte hexadecimal literal that cannot fit in ulong.
Solution: Replace it with 8-byte mock sentinel word 0x494E565F484F5431UL.
Rejected Alternatives: Splitting marker into another word would perturb existing 64-byte mock span layout. Keeping literal would fail compile.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime us. Removes hard C# compile blocker before Unity import.
Decision 019 - Probe Verification While Unity Is Locked
Problem: open Unity editor owns Temp/UnityLockfile, so batch import/compile cannot prove new files.
Solution: Use Unity's bundled Mono/Roslyn compiler with current Unity references and probe DLLs under Temp/ to compile SHINOBU contracts, memory jobs, runtime, and editor facade. This is not replacement for Unity import, but it catches syntax/API errors in edited files.
Rejected Alternatives: Killing active editor risks developer state. Reporting dotnet success alone is false because generated csproj excludes new SHINOBU files.
Problem: Final dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj retries hung after Roslyn probes and left dotnet processes consuming CPU without compiler output.
Solution: Kill only dotnet processes spawned by timed-out verification attempts and record timeout separately from successful Roslyn probes.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving orphaned build processes would waste developer hardware. Treating timeout as compile error would be inaccurate because no compiler diagnostics were emitted.
Scalability potential: None; verification hygiene only.
Problem: runtime/editor files still contained SHINOBU_78 identity strings and 0x53483738u, which would misroute telemetry identity, host naming, and fatal-message forensics for Agent 73.
Solution: Replace every SHINOBU_78 marker in SHINOBU_73 code path with SHINOBU_73 and set SystemHash to 0x53483733u. Keep dump file as task-mandated Dump_INTEGRITY_SURGEON.bin.

Problem: After identity patch, machine already had active dotnet/csc processes and reported 100% CPU load.
Solution: Do not launch another build or Roslyn probe in this pass. Record static audits and leave compile state as PENDING UNITY VERIFICATION until compiler lane is free.

Problem: previous self-audit listed Vault handles 70873..70881 but omitted later ModQuarantineBuffer handle 70882.
Solution: Append LOG self-audit update that lists all active SHINOBU handles: states, targets, results, rollback bytes, mock inventory, telemetry, runtime state, AUP snapshot, CSV scratch, and mod quarantine.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving old list would make Vault-sovereignty audit incomplete even though code requests buffer correctly.
Problem: later static audit showed runtime/editor files had reverted to stale SHINOBU_78 identity after Loop 9 patch, likely from concurrent file activity in shared workspace.
Solution: Re-apply identity repair and perform delayed 10-second code-only readback before reporting. Record event instead of silently overwriting history.
Rejected Alternatives: Marking task as clean from first patch was rejected because readback contradicted it. Making files read-only was rejected because it would sabotage concurrent agent/user edits.
Problem: Runtime PublishDesync copied MemorySentinelResultDTO.Flags directly into MemoryDesyncSignal.Flags. two flag domains are not bit-compatible; ResultFlagMismatch uses bit 1, which is MemoryDesyncSignal.FlagFatal. healed rollback could therefore be routed as fatal evidence.

Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw result-bit passthrough was rejected because it corrupts typed SignalBus contract. Adding second result-flags field to signal was rejected because it would require wider contract change and is unnecessary for current Watchdog lane.
Problem: Once CPU load dropped, fresh runtime/editor Roslyn probe still failed because it linked current SHINOBU source against stale pre-import Library/ScriptAssemblies/Hecton8.Core.dll. Solution: Record contracts/memory probe success as valid for current SHINOBU DTOs/jobs, and classify runtime/editor probe failure as Unity-import boundary evidence, not SHINOBU code compile diagnostic. authoritative next step remains Unity import/compile after active editor releases project.
Rejected Alternatives: Building local stubs for SignalBus, HomeostasisBrain, or GlobalRegistry was rejected because it would create fake compile evidence. Killing open Unity editor was rejected because it risks developer state.
Scalability potential: None; verification boundary only.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime us. Probe retry was limited to source validation and did not spawn extra compilers while CPU was saturated.

Rationale_SHINOBU_74
Status: GPU_PAGE_DEARLIE_RNG_FRAMECLOCK_DETERMINISTIC_BURST_TRIANGLE_PULSE_SQDIST_QUALITY_CADENCE_INTERPOLATOR_TELEMETRY_ASMDEF_SPLIT_HPHI_ARRAY_PURGE_ORPHAN_META_PURGED_GLOBAL_SHADER_CONSUMERS_MATRIX_PURGED_STATIC_VERIFIED_BUILD_PENDING
Evidence Class: STATIC_SOURCE after asmdef/H-PHI and shader-consumer matrix purge. Last narrow runtime C# build passed before this patch and is now stale for latest code. Unity import, Burst runtime, shader import, Play Mode, profiler, and Frame Debugger evidence still absent.
Initial Technical Boundary
Problem: 50,000 bioluminescent flora instances cannot be synchronized through Unity Light, per-renderer material mutation, or material instance churn without breaking batching and frame time.
Solution: Build deterministic presentation fake: packed uint emission colors, Burst oscillator, aligned unmanaged DTOs, AUP-safe pulse math, and GlobalQualityWeight continuum that blends individual waves into 4 global shader pulses.
Rejected Alternatives: Unity Light components, Material.SetColor, renderer.material, MaterialPropertyBlock on standard flora geometry, per-plant GameObjects, runtime CSV/string parsers, and binary quality switches.
Scalability potential: Low uses 4 global sync colors and low cadence; Middle blends group pulses with sparse individual pages; High processes full spatial waves for active flora pages; Ultra keeps richer pulse overlays and damage/O2 harmonics while preserving packed buffer output.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350, expected gain comes from preserving SRP batching and replacing object/material mutation with one native buffer path. Exact frame-time savings are PENDING VERIFICATION.
DTO Layout Commitments
Problem: Runtime DTOs feeding Burst/GPU must be stable on ARM64 and not trigger CS1612 property mutation failures.
Solution: GlowStateDTO fields remain public fields only: uint PackedColor, float Phase, float Frequency, uint SpeciesHash for 16 bytes. SyncPulseDTO uses double3 OriginAUP, float WaveSpeed, uint ColorOverride for 32 bytes.
Rejected Alternatives: auto-properties, Pack=1, managed colors, UnityEngine.Color, runtime bool, strings, arrays, and class wrappers.
Scalability potential: compact DTOs keep Low hardware cache-friendly; Ultra can add separate presentation-only buffers instead of bloating primary DTOs.
Hardware Impact: Aligned 16/32-byte records reduce cache-line waste and avoid ARM64 misaligned loads. Exact microsecond gain is static estimate only until Burst profiling.
Continuous Glow Budget Fix
Problem: active runtime used binary Dear Lie gate through _dearLieOnlyActive and UseDearLieOnly, keyed from SystemHealthIndex01 > 0.85. That violated SHINOBU_74 because actual scalability authority is GlobalQualityWeight, and transition from 50,000 spatial waves to 4 global pulses must be continuous.
Solution: Removed binary gate and added _globalQualityWeight, _individualGlowWeight01, _dearLieBlend01, and _scheduledGpuColorCount. RefreshGlobalQualityWeight() reads HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight; ResolveIndividualGlowWeight() smoothsteps quality/stress continuum; ResolveScheduledGlowCount() maps result to 4..50000 job iterations. Burst job receives GlobalQualityWeight, fades expensive spatial pulses by IndividualGlowWeight01, boosts 4 Dear Lie groups by DearLieBlend01, and only uploads ...TRIMMED_LINE
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping _dearLieOnlyActive; hardware tier enums; if low tier then skip all switches; point lights; material swaps; per-renderer MPB updates.
Scalability potential: Low uses exactly 4 global pulses at GlobalQualityWeight 0.1. Middle schedules partial per-plant page count with smooth polynomial curve. High schedules near-full spatial waves. Ultra keeps same 50,000 limit but spends saved cycles on pulse overlays, damage flicker, oxygen warning, and bloom-visible HDR emission.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350-class silicon, 0.1 quality path statically avoids up to 49,996 per-plant iterations and skips bulk packed-color upload. Exact frame-time savings require Unity Profiler/Frame Debugger capture and are not fabricated here.
Verification And Self-Audit
Problem: system needed proof that batching killer was removed without inventing performance numbers.
Solution: Ran static scans for forbidden tokens in assigned biolum runtime/editor files, re-read SHINOBU_74 prompt count from CURRENT_BATCH.md, and compiled both runtime/editor C# projects with --no-dependencies to isolate this assembly.

Problem: system needed proof that batching killer was removed without inventing performance numbers.
Solution: Ran static scans for forbidden tokens in assigned biolum runtime/editor files, re-read SHINOBU_74 prompt count from CURRENT_BATCH.md, and compiled both runtime/editor C# projects with --no-dependencies to isolate this assembly.
Rejected Alternatives: Reporting completion from source inspection only; using full dependency build timeout as false failure; editing unrelated core systems.
Hardware Impact: Static audit passed. Earlier runtime/editor C# compiles are historical and predate asmdef/H-PHI patch. Unity import, fresh assembly build, Play Mode, GPU timing, and Frame Debugger evidence are still pending, so exact measured microseconds remain pending.
Problem: first pass fixed visible binary Dear Lie violation but still left three forensic gaps: Burst aliasing proof was implicit, profile binary hydration used native-endian float reads, and job batch size was magic literal instead of cache-line contract.
Solution: Added NoAlias to every disjoint BiolumVisualSyncJob NativeArray lane, kept read-only lanes marked ReadOnly, NoAlias, replaced MemoryMarshal.Read profile hydration with explicit little-endian byte assembly plus math.asfloat, and named schedule batch as BiolumJobInnerLoopBatchCount = 64 with cache rationale.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting Burst to infer aliasing from DataVault BufferIDs; assuming all future import tools are little-endian by accident; keeping 64 as unexplained scheduling literal; claiming profiler savings without Burst Inspector evidence.
Hardware Impact: Compile passed after correction. Runtime speedup is not measured here. practical impact is removing blockers to NEON/AVX vectorization and preventing silent profile corruption on non-native endian readers.
Problem: polish mandate asked for all runtime arrays to be in Vault. earlier implementation still had two cold managed bridge arrays, so caveat was real and had to be removed rather than documented forever.
Solution: Persistent simulation/upload data remains DataVault-owned through VaultBufferHandles. managed Vector416 shader bridge was replaced by Matrix4x4 _dearLieGroupMatrix and _GlobalBiolumDearLieGroups. managed byte16384 CSV staging buffer was removed; CSV reload now reads directly into BiolumCsvScratch.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping shader array support because it was convenient; parsing CSV from managed strings; claiming zero private arrays before removing them.
Problem: binary ledger showed Data/Visuals/Biolum_Profiles.bin had reader, but no scene/prefab/bootstrap proof that BiolumPulseSyncRuntime would actually exist in clean play session. binary reader with no boot path is dead integration.
Solution: Added scene-local RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(AfterSceneLoad) fallback host with atomic process ownership claim. If authored scene instance has already enabled and claimed ownership, fallback does nothing. If none exists, it creates one cold H8_BiolumPulseSyncRuntime host and attaches runtime. hot 50,000-plant path remains in native buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing global Core bootstrap, scene/prefab assets, introducing sibling-domain dependency, storing static runtime instance pointer, using scene FindObject probes, or relying on documentation that scene object will exist. Per-plant GameObjects remain rejected; this is one cold scene service host.
Problem: first runtime-host pass used s_runtimeInstance and Awake() duplicate suppression. That matched common Unity code, but it violated project rule forbidding classic singleton/self-registration patterns.
Solution: Removed static runtime instance pointer and deleted Awake(). Ownership is now single int s_runtimeClaimed process claim reset at subsystem registration, acquired in OnEnable() with Interlocked.CompareExchange, and released through ReleaseRuntimeOwnerClaim(). claim does not expose instance accessor and does not become service locator; real update/late-frame participation still goes through GlobalRegistry.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping s_runtimeInstance; using FindAnyObjectByType in runtime; moving ownership into Core bootstrap without authorization; letting duplicate hosts race DataVault locks.
Scalability potential: No change to quality math. This preserves compile-wall and lifecycle discipline while keeping low/middle/high/ultra glow continuum unchanged.
Post-Host Compile Wall
Problem: After runtime-host edit, isolated Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-Editor builds could not resolve Temp\bin\Debug\Hecton8.Core.dll. minimal Hecton8.Core.csproj compile was required to distinguish SHINOBU failure from dependency failure.
Solution: Ran minimal Core dependency check once. It fails outside SHINOBU domain at Assets/_Project/Scripts/Core/GlobalSignals.cs(1119,26) with CS0266: cannot implicitly convert void* to T*. Work stopped there and status was marked as blocked by Core dependency, not silently reported as clean compile.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing Core without authorization, repeatedly rebuilding into same known dependency failure, or reverting SHINOBU code to hide pre-existing Core compile wall.
Problem: Static source review found render-path disconnect after CPU packed-color work. BiolumPulseSyncRuntime uploaded _BiolumGpuColorBuffer, but Hecton_IndirectVegetation.shader did not consume that buffer. second defect existed in global fallback: Burst path writes four valid Dear Lie states, while _GlobalBiolumParams.x could still publish _activeStateCount up to 16, letting shaders sample zero-filled global slots.
Solution: Added _publishedGlobalStateCount so shader globals publish actual valid state count. After Burst job, that count is four. indirect vegetation shader now declares _BiolumGpuColorBuffer, decodes RGB10_A2 uint colors by sourceInstanceIndex, and blends authored glow toward synced runtime glow only when real uploaded GPU page exists.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving GPU buffer as dead upload bandwidth; switching to material properties or per-renderer MPBs; sampling all 50,000 packed colors after partial upload; publishing _activeStateCount while only four global states are valid.
Problem: shader bridge still had cold-start hazard. GraphicsBuffer can exist before any packed color page has been uploaded. Publishing desired schedule count or default individual weight would let shader read uninitialized GPU memory during first frame. desired scheduled count can also exceed actual upload count because upload is clamped by _activeGlowInstanceCount and vault buffer length.
Solution: Added _publishedGpuColorCount, initialized and reset to zero whenever GPU page becomes invalid. TryUploadGpuColorBufferFromLockedVault() sets it to exact count passed to UnlockBufferAfterWrite. UploadShaderScalars() publishes this actual uploaded count in _GlobalBiolumParams.w and publishes individual shader weight only when uploaded count is greater than four Dear Lie groups. shader renamed guard to packedBufferCount and refuses reads outside that exact range.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting GraphicsBuffer default contents; exposing _scheduledGpuColorCount before upload completion; keeping stale front-buffer reads after DataVault handle refresh; forcing full 50,000 upload to avoid count tracking.
Problem: indirect vegetation shader's global fallback picked _GlobalBiolumStates by position-derived noise. original SHINOBU task requires four Dear Lie colors to be selected by species hash modulo 4. Position selection is visually plausible, but it can make identical species disagree and it drifts from batch contract.
Solution: Added biolumSyncGroup varying. vertex path derives it from finite-guarded TemplateIndex modulo four, with stable finite-guarded Type + Variation fallback when no template is authored. ResolveIndirectVegetationGlobalBiolum now receives this group and selects global state by group modulo active count. High-tier overdrive still uses local position and time for shimmer, but base Dear Lie color is species/template-group stable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping position noise; adding material keyword or per-renderer property; demanding new cross-domain species hash buffer from world renderer; widening runtime DTOs outside SHINOBU domain.
Problem: Mock predator proximity firing used custom deterministic hash. That avoided UnityEngine.Random, but mandate explicitly requires Unity.Mathematics.Random seeded from sector/frame state for deterministic rollback-compatible random streams.
Solution: Added CreateDeterministicRandom(uint sectorHash, uint frameCounter, uint salt), seeding Unity.Mathematics.Random from biome/profile sector hash plus _frameCounter through default plus InitState(seed) rather than gameplay-path new constructor. AdvanceMockPredatorSignal now uses that struct RNG for roll, origin angle, radius, and wave radius. This remains value type and does not allocate heap memory.
Rejected Alternatives: UnityEngine.Random, System.Random, custom hash-only random stream, or managed random objects.
Problem: scheduled glow count already came from continuous GlobalQualityWeight, but final count mapping used raw multiplication. mandate explicitly asks for math.lerp, math.step, and polynomial curves to express quality shedding.
Solution: ResolveScheduledGlowCount now computes activeWeight = SmoothStep01(weight) * math.step(0.0001f, weight) and then uses math.lerp(4, 50000, activeWeight). This keeps near-zero path collapsed to four global Dear Lie groups while preserving continuous scaling once quality/stress permits individual sampling.
Rejected Alternatives: Raw linear multiplication; binary quality branch; hardware-tier enum; always scheduling full 50,000 because GPU buffer exists.
Problem: global polish mandate mentions HZB occlusion for 50,000 kelp plants. SHINOBU_74 does not own draw-list culling or matrix dispatch; editing that path would violate domain boundary.
Solution: Static source check shows HectonIndirectVegetationRenderer.cs owns BRG/indirect vegetation culling, and FloraCulling.compute declares _HectonDepthPyramid, _HectonOcclusionEnabled, depth bias, and visible-instance append buffers. SHINOBU's packed color buffer is presentation data consumed by existing indirect vegetation shader, not draw-submission path.
Rejected Alternatives: Duplicating HZB culling in glow runtime; adding CPU AABB culling inside SHINOBU; touching world renderer without authorization.
Problem: first species-group correction added separate TEXCOORD22 scalar for biolumSyncGroup. Functionally correct, but wasteful on mobile shader path because existing TEXCOORD21 spatial pulse offset had enough scalar capacity.
Solution: Replaced two scalar varyings with half2 biolumPulseData : TEXCOORD21; .x carries spatial pulse offset and .y carries four-state Dear Lie sync group. Spore sparkle, local pulse phase, and global Dear Lie state selection now read from this packed pair.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping dedicated varying for one 0..3 group id; deriving group again in fragment from world position; adding material keyword.
Problem: BiolumPulseTelemetryEntry.ActiveGlowingInstances reported _scheduledGpuColorCount. After adding _publishedGpuColorCount, scheduled count can exceed what shader is allowed to sample if upload has not completed or GPU page is invalid.
Solution: Telemetry now records shader-visible glow count: _publishedGpuColorCount only when valid uploaded page exists and exceeds four Dear Lie groups; otherwise it reports SyncGroupCount = 4.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving scheduled count in blackbox; adding another telemetry field and keeping misleading old one; blocking frame to force publication before telemetry.
Problem: _frameCounter advanced inside RecordTelemetry(). That made simulation-visible frame state depend on how many blackbox entries were written. NaN/fault path can call RecordTelemetry() outside normal Tick tail, which would perturb deterministic RNG seeding, shader frame clock, and mock predator FrameStamp.
Solution: Added AdvanceSimulationFrameCounter() and call it exactly once in Tick() after delta sanitization and before RNG/signal work. RecordTelemetry() now records current frame without incrementing. MockPredatorProximitySignal.FrameStamp now uses current frame rather than predicting telemetry-incremented next frame.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping telemetry as frame owner; deriving frame from Unity Time.frameCount; adding Core dependency for new frame service; blocking fault telemetry until next Tick.
Problem: BiolumVisualSyncJob still used FloatMode.Fast. job mutates GlowStateDTO.Phase and packed GPU color DTOs, and those values are recorded in telemetry and can be replayed or compared during rollback investigations. Fast-math freedom is wrong default for this stateful visual synchronization kernel.
Solution: Changed only BiolumVisualSyncJob to BurstCompile(CompileSynchronously = true, FloatMode = FloatMode.Deterministic, FloatPrecision = FloatPrecision.Standard). shader-side presentation overkill remains outside this CPU state authority.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping FloatMode.Fast; hand-quantizing every sine path before writing DTOs; moving phase state into shader time only and losing deterministic CPU telemetry.
Problem: After C# edits, compile check was justified. first CPU guard read was below 50% and no dotnet/csc process was active, but narrow build returned exit 1 with empty quiet/errors-only output.
Solution: Did not guess. Waited for spawned dotnet/csc processes to exit, then rechecked guard state. CPU remained at 99%, so no diagnostic rerun was launched.
Rejected Alternatives: Running repeated builds while CPU was saturated; claiming compile pass from empty failed build; editing unrelated Core files.
Scalability potential: Not runtime scalability. This preserves build-throttle rule and prevents compile-wall churn during parallel-agent work.
Problem: BiolumVisualSyncJob still paid math.sin inside 50,000-instance path for base oscillator, damage flicker chaos, and O2 heartbeat. visual requirement is believable glow pulse, not trigonometric truth.
Solution: Replaced per-plant sine pulses with ResolveSmoothedTrianglePulse01(), triangle wave shaped by cubic smoothstep polynomial. Replaced damage chaos sine with deterministic uint hash noise seeded by instance index, damage frame stamp, and fixed time bucket. Replaced O2 heartbeat sine with same smoothed triangle phase.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping sine per instance; moving all pulse work to Unity Lights; adding shader/material variants; adding lookup texture that would need streaming/warmup proof.
Problem: Spatial pulse propagation and damage flicker still used math.length() inside active 50,000-instance job. Exact Euclidean distance is not required for emissive ripple/flicker presentation fake.
Solution: Replaced distance sqrt with squared-distance math. Spatial pulses compare distanceSq against squared wave radius and derive shell width in squared units. Damage falloff uses lengthsq / radiusSq shaped by SmoothStep01. Both paths now finite-check localized AUP deltas and clamp denominators with math.max(..., 0.0001f).
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping sqrt per plant; reducing active pulse count only; moving ripple truth to physics; using texture lookup that would need shader warmup/import proof.
Problem: individual count scaled with GlobalQualityWeight, but normal scheduling cadence was still 0 seconds, meaning per-frame job scheduling even when quality had collapsed to four Dear Lie groups. mandate explicitly calls for update frequency to shed toward 5Hz under low quality.
Solution: Added ResolveUpdateCadenceSeconds(globalQualityWeight, overloadHoldSeconds). It uses SmoothStepRange01, math.lerp, and continuous overload scalar. Low quality maps toward 0.2s (5Hz), high quality maps toward per-frame, and overload pressure blends toward existing 15Hz interval. UploadShaderScalars() publishes same cadence to _GlobalBiolumClock.y.
Rejected Alternatives: Fixed per-frame scheduling; binary low-end hardware branch; keeping overload as hard boolean switch.
Problem: previous quality-cadence pass still had only static evidence and older empty-output build failure in log. That was not acceptable after code changes.
Solution: Rechecked build guard, waited until no dotnet/csc process was active and CPU was below user's 50% limit, then ran one narrow runtime build only: dotnet build Assembly-CSharp.csproj --no-restore --no-dependencies -v:minimal -m:1 /p:UseSharedCompilation=false /p:BuildInParallel=false /clp:ErrorsOnly. Result: PASS, 0 warnings, 0 errors, 00:00:16.04.
Rejected Alternatives: Running dotnet rebuild; running full dependency build; launching editor build without fresh need; hiding earlier failed quiet attempt.
Scalability potential: Not runtime tier change. This confirms runtime C# edits compile in isolated Assembly-CSharp path while Unity import/profiler evidence remains pending.
Problem: runtime still carried two private managed bridge arrays: _managedStates Vector416 for Shader.SetGlobalVectorArray and _csvWorkerScratch byte16384 for CSV file staging. That undermined H-PHI claim and left 16-slot shader array where actual Dear Lie contract is four groups.
Solution: Removed _managedStates, _GlobalBiolumStatesId, and every Shader.SetGlobalVectorArray call. four Dear Lie groups now live in Matrix4x4 _dearLieGroupMatrix and are published as _GlobalBiolumDearLieGroups (float4x4) to shader. Removed CSV worker thread and private byte array. CSV hot reload now locks BiolumCsvScratch, reads file directly into vault-owned NativeArray via Span over native pointer, and parses that same buffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping managed Vector4 because Unity's vector-array API was convenient; keeping byte because FileStream.Read(byte) was familiar; expanding Core with new buffer ID; duplicating shader state through both array and matrix paths.
Compile Wall Assembly Split
Problem: SHINOBU runtime lived in Assembly-CSharp and editor facade lived in broad Hecton8.Editor assembly path. That contradicted compile-wall mandate even though source itself avoided sibling gameplay references.
Solution: Added Assets/_Project/Scripts/VFX/Bioluminescence/Hecton8.VFX.Bioluminescence.Runtime.asmdef and moved editor facade under Assets/_Project/Scripts/VFX/Bioluminescence/Editor with Hecton8.VFX.Bioluminescence.Editor.asmdef. editor assembly references only SHINOBU runtime assembly and Unity.Mathematics. Runtime references Core.Contracts/Core/Core.Memory and Unity Burst/Collections/Jobs/Mathematics/Profiling; no AI, fauna, combat, world, physics, or sibling VFX assembly is referenced.
Rejected Alternatives: Modifying global Hecton8.Editor.asmdef; leaving files in predefined assemblies; adding direct references to flora/world renderer code.
Hardware Impact: Compile-wall hygiene only. Unity import/build proof is still pending because new asmdefs require Unity project regeneration.
Problem: After moving BioluminescenceTunerWindow.cs under Assets/_Project/Scripts/VFX/Bioluminescence/Editor, old tracked Assets/_Project/Scripts/Editor/BioluminescenceTunerWindow.cs.meta remained on disk without .cs file. Unity can preserve stale script GUID and import noise from that orphan.
Solution: Deleted only orphaned .meta file. live editor facade keeps its domain-local .meta and lives under Hecton8.VFX.Bioluminescence.Editor.asmdef.
Rejected Alternatives: Recreating old script path; leaving dead GUID for Unity import; touching unrelated editor files already dirty from other agents.
Scalability potential: Not runtime tier change. It protects compile/import hygiene for SHINOBU editor facade.
Problem: Runtime stopped publishing _GlobalBiolumStates16 after H-PHI purge, but active coral, kelp, sargassum, procedural-bio, GPUI, and leviathan shaders still sampled that retired vector array. That would leave old consumers reading stale/zero global pulse data while SHINOBU published only _GlobalBiolumDearLieGroups.
Solution: Converted every active biolum shader consumer under Assets/_Project/Art/Shaders from _GlobalBiolumStates16 to float4x4 _GlobalBiolumDearLieGroups, and clamped active global state count to four rows. runtime remains single publisher through Shader.SetGlobalMatrix.
Rejected Alternatives: Reintroducing Shader.SetGlobalVectorArray; publishing both legacy and matrix globals; touching material instances; leaving stale fauna/flora shader reads because they were outside narrow first shader file.

Decision 00 - Scope Boundary
Problem: Batch prompt references other agents' concrete types that may not exist or may be concurrently edited.
Solution: Implement SHINOBU_75-owned DTOs, jobs, and facade APIs under UI/presentation; communicate through owned unmanaged buffers and future seam contracts instead of hard references to Anomaly Director, Radar, Audio, or Terminal concrete classes.
Rejected Alternatives: Directly calling Agent 48/29/28 classes would create compile walls and cross-domain dependencies.
Scalability potential: Interface-free static kernels can be called from weak-device and high-end paths with GlobalQualityWeight.

Decision 01 - Binary Table Ownership
Problem: Runtime must read Assets/_Project/Data/UI/GlitchTable.bytes but text scrambling cannot touch managed strings or TextAsset hot paths.
Solution: DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime loads binary table once into vault byte buffer, sanitizes glyph bytes, hashes table, and falls back to GlitchTable.GenerateEmergencyMockGlitchTable() on missing/failed IO.
Rejected Alternatives: TextAsset.bytes and File.ReadAllBytes allocate managed arrays; per-frame Resources lookup is banned.
Scalability potential: Low reuses table only for sparse text swaps; Middle/High/Ultra spend same resident table on denser substitutions and shader seed offsets.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids per-frame IO and GC; table access is 64-byte pointer indexing, expected under 1 us for mock span.

Solution: GlitchStateDTO is explicit 16 bytes with public fields and AsRef(void*); ScrambledCharacterDTO is requested 4-byte mapping record; all resident runtime arrays use DataVault buffers with NativeArrayOptions.UninitializedMemory except telemetry/cursor clear paths.

Hardware Impact: Expected gain is bounded lookup work and aligned linear memory access; microsecond estimate pending source implementation and compile.
Problem: runtime had low-level XOR jobs but no public path binding lookup, player-progress mask, and caller-owned decrypted output.
Solution: Added TryBuildProgressDecryptionMask, LocRegistry.TrySetLoreDecryptionMask, LocRegistry.TryScheduleLoreDecryption, and BabelDictionaryStore.TryScheduleLoreDecryption. Missing required lore bits generate deterministic 16-byte mask; all collected bits clear mask to zero, revealing clean UTF-8.
Rejected Alternatives: Decrypting into managed string, returning heap-owned byte, or letting PDA/UI layer poke private Babel buffers. These would violate zero-GC and ownership boundaries.
Decision 03: Verification Boundary
Problem: Full compile is forbidden while CPU is under load and dotnet/csc already run.
Solution: Performed static source scans, direct binary header/length probe, and VerifyBinaryHygiene.py report generation. Deferred dotnet compile until guard is clear.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching another build into 100% CPU or reporting compile success without evidence.
Scalability potential: Verification remains cheap and does not create additional build contention while 20+ agents are active.
Problem: previous pass left pointer safety invariants implicit and allowed public pointer-backed lore decrypt scheduler to accept uncreated mask even though Unity job safety can reject unconstructed NativeArray fields at schedule time.
Solution: Require created progress mask for TryScheduleLoreDecryption; clean text is represented by existing 16-byte zero mask. Add three-part safety comments to raw pointer job fields and annotate two Complete() calls as explicit structural sync points.
Rejected Alternatives: Scheduling with default mask and relying on NativeArray.IsCreated inside Execute was rejected because scheduler can validate containers before Burst executes. Removing Complete() calls outright was rejected because CSV/staged-locale mutation must not race active UTF-8 reader jobs.
Hardware Impact: Estimated low-end i3/MX350 impact is fewer schedule-time safety failures and no extra source copy before XOR decrypt. Runtime microsecond delta is unchanged for valid calls; measured proof absent.
Decision 05: Compile Wall Caveat
Problem: polish mandate demands no sibling Runtime assembly references, but Babel currently sits inside monolithic Hecton8.Core asmdef, and that asmdef already references multiple sibling runtime assemblies.
Solution: Record compile-wall violation as pre-existing architecture debt and avoid mutating Hecton8.Core.asmdef from Babel-local task.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing 16 sibling references from Hecton8.Core.asmdef was rejected because it would be cross-domain integration operation with high compile break risk. Creating new asmdef around existing root-level LocRegistry.cs was rejected because it would change ownership and public assembly boundaries mid-batch.
Hardware Impact: No frame-time gain now; preserving compile wall requires dedicated integration pass, not blind local edit.
Problem: BabelDictionaryStore.TryScheduleLoreDecryption schedules job reading from MMF/Vault raw pointer. Without store-owned reader fence, CloseFile() could release pointer during reload/shutdown before job completes.
Solution: Add _activeLoreReadHandle and combine scheduled lore decrypt handles into it. CloseFile() completes fence before releasing MMF/Vault pointers; completed fences are cleared non-blockingly on later schedules.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting callers to never reload while jobs run was rejected because it is undocumented temporal contract. Copying source bytes into intermediate output before scheduling was rejected because it doubles bandwidth and defeats MMF.

Rationale_SHINOBU_78
Status: PENDING VERIFICATION
Initial Boundary
Problem: SHINOBU_78 duplicates existing memory-sentinel functionality while adding mod-protection and future command-kernel opcode reservation pressure.
Solution: Treat existing MemorySentinelRuntime as primary integration point and only add missing integrity/quarantine surfaces after source readback.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting second sentinel would create two schedulers hashing same vault ranges and produce false desyncs under parallel agents.
Scalability potential: Low = player/economy only; Middle = base integrity and registry hashes; High = richer telemetry; Ultra = broader validation density without binary quality switches.
Hardware Impact: Avoiding duplicate runtime scheduler preserves estimated 20-60 us/frame on i3/MX350 and prevents extra DataVault buffers.
Problem: Mandate selection before code.
Solution: Use eight directly relevant mandates: Zero-GC, Native Jobs, ARM64 struct layout, SoA inventory, AUP determinism, floating origin precision, execution phases, typed signal lanes.
Rejected Alternatives: Reading graphics/audio mandates would dilute domain; using dated archive reports as authority would violate current AGENTS hierarchy.
Scalability potential: Mandates force continuous GlobalQualityWeight cadence rather than low/ultra toggle.
Hardware Impact: Bounded job and layout rules protect Quest/MX350 from unaligned access and managed heap stalls.
Decision 01 - Mod quarantine cannot weaken base data
Problem: AppendExistingBuffer was adding TargetFlagAllowModPrefix to every protected DataVault span. In modded session, malicious write could plant MODP at start of base inventory/AUP memory and make sentinel skip that target.
Solution: Add separate 64-byte MemorySentinelModQuarantineSpan seeded with MODP, allocate it as ModQuarantineBuffer, and make it only runtime target with TargetFlagAllowModPrefix. Base buffers now append only TargetFlagActive plus their critical/AUP/inventory flags.
Rejected Alternatives: Global mod-mode disable was rejected because it sacrifices base-game integrity. String/path mod whitelists were rejected because they are managed and forgeable. Per-buffer reflection metadata was rejected because it invents dependencies on systems that are not in this domain.
Scalability potential: Low = one quarantine span and player/economy hashes; Middle = more mod spans by DataVault ID; High = richer per-mod telemetry; Ultra = larger quarantined UGC surface while first-party memory remains fully protected.
Hardware Impact: Adds one 64-byte hash target only when scheduled. Low-end i3/MX350 cost estimate is 1-3 us on validation frames, while closing integrity bypass that would otherwise invalidate sentinel.
Decision 02 - Future command-kernel opcode reservation
Problem: Current mod command opcodes use 1-8, but no guard stopped public mods or kernels from occupying future command-kernel range.
Solution: Reserve 0x7800..0x78FF for both opcode and target IDs. ModCommandDispatcher rejects that range at kernel registration and security-gate validation. FutureSystemSeamContracts exposes same range and validation helper for seam auditors.
Rejected Alternatives: Waiting for Agent 80 was rejected because mods can ship against current API surface. Adding dependency from ModdingAPI to Hecton8.Global.Contracts was rejected to avoid asmdef compile-wall expansion.
Scalability potential: Low = hard reject reserved IDs; Middle = seam validator consumes range constants; High = future command kernel binds range without API break; Ultra = generated contract tables can expand inside reserved band.

Date: 2026-05-19
Agent: SHINOBU_79
Status: IMPLEMENTED; STATIC VERIFIED; UNITY COMPILE NOT LAUNCHED
Decision 00 - QA watchdog boundary
Problem: task requires headless 10km endurance bot, but other agents own input, AUP rebase, SystemHealthIndex, and crash dump systems.
Solution: Use local QA watchdog runtime with unmanaged DTOs and mock-compatible interfaces/structs. Integrate through cold activation and stable DTO surfaces only; do not create hard dependencies on unfinished concrete systems.
Rejected Alternatives: Player-prefab MonoBehaviour autoplay was rejected because it couples QA to hierarchy and XR/Input Manager. Direct calls into Agent 30/33 systems were rejected because those contracts are not proven current.
Scalability potential: Low uses sparse sampling and compact CSV rows. Middle increases probe cadence. High records richer slope metrics. Ultra spends saved overhead on denser telemetry and editor visual forensics.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 expected gain is avoiding manual scene replay and avoiding GC-induced false leak positives; hot-path budget target under 100 microseconds with CSV cadence throttled.
Decision 01 - File output strategy
Problem: CSV telemetry can become leak if it formats strings or opens files per frame.
Solution: Keep persistent FileStream and preallocated byte staging buffer. Write ASCII numerics manually. Headers are cold-path only.
Rejected Alternatives: File.AppendAllText, string.Format, interpolation, StreamWriter, and per-row string construction were rejected as managed allocation hazards.
Scalability potential: Low writes less often. Middle writes standard cadence. High/Ultra can increase telemetry frequency while preserving same staging path.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoids GC spikes from managed logging; expected save is variable but any per-frame string allocation is eliminated from watchdog-owned path.
Decision 02 - DTO layout
Problem: WatchdogStateDTO and TelemetrySnapshotDTO must survive ARM64 alignment and NativeArray/Burst use.
Solution: Sequential unmanaged structs with explicit fields matching prompt byte layouts; no properties; no Pack=1; unsafe layout asserts in editor/test entry points.
Rejected Alternatives: Auto-properties, classes, bool fields, and packed structs were rejected because they create copies, managed metadata risk, or misaligned ARM64 reads.
Scalability potential: Same layout across tiers. Ultra can add separate extended telemetry DTOs rather than bloating truth structs.
Hardware Impact: Stable 40B/16B records reduce cache waste and prevent ARM64 unaligned penalties.
Decision 03 - Archive binary fallback
Problem: Task 01 required locating qa_waypoints.h8bin/endurance_profiles.bin layouts in Archive Batch005-007, but targeted scans found no matching binary names or rationale lines.
Solution: Treat missing archive payload as expected cold-path failure and keep GenerateEmergencyMockRoute() as boot fallback: four 32-byte waypoint records with 16-byte aligned AUP payloads covering 10km path.

Rejected Alternatives: New MonoBehaviour bot or renaming every type was rejected because it increases prefab/meta risk and compile surface without functional gain.
Problem: Writing only BufferID.ShinobuInputCurrentDto satisfies byte contract, but current InputDispatcher consumes gameplay automation from PhysicsDeterminismSignals.TryConsumeLatestInputOverride().
Solution: Keep unmanaged DataVault write, then mirror same bytes into PhysicsDeterminismSignals.PublishInputOverride using Unity frame counter so KCC consumes it without touching XR or Input Manager.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct XR device emulation, Player prefab scripts, or adding QA dependency to Input assembly were rejected as hierarchy-coupled or assembly-hostile.
Problem: watchdog previously published SHI stress only; it did not mathematically force GlobalQualityWeight through required 0.1-to-1.0 thermal recovery transition.
Solution: Apply HomeostasisBrain.SetForcedGlobalQualityWeightForTuner() on 600s loop: 300s clamp at 0.1, 60s smoothstep recovery to 1.0, remainder at full quality; release override on finish/destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Binary low/high tier flags and one-shot quality writes were rejected because project forbids dichotomy and needs transition stress.
Problem: Legacy QAEnduranceWatchdogBot also responded to H8_QA_ENDURANCE_10KM and -h8QaEndurance*, causing two bots to fight over automation when SHINOBU_79 launches.

Rejected Alternatives: Leaving both active or deleting legacy file was rejected. Leaving both creates nondeterminism; deletion risks unrelated QA callers.
Problem: project rules forbid launching dotnet/Unity builds while CPU exceeds 50 percent or csc.exe is active.
Solution: latest guard sample is CPU=100.00 percent with csc.exe count 0, so compilation remains blocked by policy on CPU load. separate target scan found no Hecton8.QA.Headless.csproj or sln entry for these QA Headless files. Static scans covered forbidden logging APIs, properties, Pack=1, AutoPlayer, asmdef references, generated target presence, and active code paths.
Rejected Alternatives: Forcing broad dotnet build was rejected because it would not verify ungenerated QA Headless assembly and user explicitly ordered not to launch dotnet build until necessary.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoids compounding compiler workload or running irrelevant builds; no runtime microsecond gain claimed.
Problem: first pass drove GlobalQualityWeight and SHI stress from fast-forwarded simulation seconds or frame count, and second pass still used unscaled tick delta. Manual batch stepping can execute hundreds of ticks per editor update, so delta-based wall time is not wall time.
Solution: Track _qualityWallSeconds from Stopwatch.GetTimestamp() deltas, clamped to 1s per sample for pause resilience. GlobalQualityWeight now clamps at 0.1 for 300 real elapsed seconds, smoothstep-recovers for 60 real elapsed seconds, then dwells at 1.0. SHI sabotage now publishes 0.95 for 10 real elapsed seconds per 60s cycle.
Rejected Alternatives: Frame-count modulo, simulation-duration timing, and manual-step delta timing were rejected because fast-forward/manual batch stepping invalidates thermal soak requirement.
Problem: first pass checked millimeter float-downcast jitter but did not explicitly implement prompt's >500m inter-frame local delta failure gate.
Solution: Store last audited double3 AUP, subtract before casting to local float3, and flag VaultFlagFatal when length(localDelta) > 500m without current MockRebaseSignal.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying only on target-relative jitter or absolute double comparisons was rejected; watchdog must catch frame-to-frame coordinate explosions.
Problem: InputDispatcher consumes automation overrides by comparing PhysicsDeterminismSignals frame against its own Time.frameCount. Publishing SHINOBU_79's fast-forward simulation frame would age out override and break Dear Lie input path.
Solution: Use Time.frameCount only for input override handshake. Movement integration, quality soak, SHI pulse duration, memory windows, and AUP audit do not use Unity Time.frameCount for state evolution.
Rejected Alternatives: Publishing simulation _frame to PhysicsDeterminismSignals was rejected because existing consumer uses engine frame age. XR/Input Manager injection was rejected again because it violates prompt.
Problem: avoidance path still paid for rich SDF normals whenever wall was detected, even while GlobalQualityWeight was clamped to 0.1 for thermal stress soak.
Solution: Feed forced GlobalQualityWeight into BotNavigationJob. Below 0.3, math.step collapses rich normal path to cheap analytic normal; above threshold, smoothstep-style polynomial blending lerps into six-sample SDF gradient.
Rejected Alternatives: Always sampling rich normal was rejected because it hides low-tier ALU shedding failures. binary hardware flag was rejected because HECTON-8 requires continuous GlobalQualityWeight math.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoidance frames avoid six extra SDF samples below 0.3 quality. Static estimate is 4-12 us saved on CPU-bound avoidance frames, unmeasured because compile/playmode was blocked.
Problem: first sabotage path could prove entry into LowTierEmergency but not clean recovery; sticky low-tier bit would make forensic CSV ambiguous.
Solution: Track whether SHINOBU_79 owns current stress pulse. When pulse ends and SHI drops below 0.9, clear VaultFlagLowTierEmergency and set VaultFlagStressRecoveryObserved plus TelemetryFlagStressRecovered.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving low-tier flag sticky was rejected because it cannot distinguish valid recovery from permanent load-shedding failure. Clearing all vault flags was rejected because it would erase unrelated memory/fatal evidence.
Problem: AUP jitter should compare intended path against engine-produced KCC AUP when that signal exists. Auditing only next waypoint is too coarse and can miss KCC output drift.
Solution: Read PhysicsDeterminismSignals.TryGetLatestKccVelocity opportunistically, reject stale samples older than two engine frames, subtract vault.CurrentAUP from BodyAup before casting to float3, then reconstruct and flag >1mm error.
Rejected Alternatives: target-waypoint-relative audit was rejected because waypoint is not bot's current intended position. Direct Gameplay/KCC assembly references were rejected because QA Headless must stay behind Core signal lanes.
Scalability potential: Low and Middle get optional real KCC output verification when available. High and Ultra can use same signal for richer postmortem without adding sibling assembly reference.
Problem: command-line parser ignored inline values when inline argument was final argv element, which can silently discard CI tuning such as -h8qaSpeed=8.
Solution: Iterate all argv entries, check inline key=value first, then check separated key value only when i + 1 exists. Apply same pattern to -h8qaTier.
Rejected Alternatives: Separated-only CLI was rejected because CI scripts commonly use inline values. Throwing on malformed args was rejected because QA activation must fail soft to safe defaults.
Problem: SHINOBU_79 originally defined local Shinobu38InputStateDTO with same 24-byte shape as InputDispatcher's InputStateDTO, then requested BufferID.ShinobuInputCurrentDto with that local type. Same-size shadow DTOs are still DataVault contract hazard because handle typing, ownership, and future ABI changes can diverge silently.
Solution: Delete local shadow DTO and request VaultBufferHandle for BufferID.ShinobuInputCurrentDto, matching InputDispatcher.EnsureDeterministicInputNativeBuffers exactly. BotNavigationJob writes canonical struct; PhysicsDeterminismSignals still receives mirrored PlayerInputState override.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping same-size local DTO was rejected because identical layout is not durable contract. Referencing Hecton8.Input.Determinism.InputStateDTO was rejected because QA Headless does not reference that sibling asmdef and Core already owns active buffer contract.
Decision 17 - Actual AUP position error, not reconstruction-only
Problem: optional KCC AUP audit measured float reconstruction error but did not flag real position mismatch between intended watchdog AUP and engine-produced BodyAup if mismatch was representable in float.
Solution: Subtract intended vault.CurrentAUP from actual BodyAup first, cast local delta to float3, and record worst of local position delta and reconstruction error. Any worst error above 1mm increments ErrorCount and sets VaultFlagActualAupJitter.
Rejected Alternatives: Reconstruction-only auditing was rejected because it proves float precision but not prompt's intended-path-versus-actual-position requirement. Absolute double comparisons were rejected because AUP rules require subtracting before float math.
Hardware Impact: Adds one local vector length on frames with KCC output; estimated 1 us on low-end CPUs, unmeasured because build/playmode remains blocked.
Problem: watchdog could reach 10km distance target under fast-forwarded simulation time before real five-minute GlobalQualityWeight clamp and one-minute recovery had elapsed. That would create false positive endurance report and skip thermal transition task exists to test. same defect affected five-minute memory leak slope window because it was advanced by simulated frame time.
